_readme: ACCEPTANCE THRESHOLDS FOR THE DEMO TRIAL OF QSMC v6.6.24.
THE OWNER EDITS THE FOUR NUMBERS BELOW BEFORE THE TRIAL STARTS and does not
touch them afterwards. A threshold moved mid-trial turns an experiment into
a story. tools/analyze_trial.py reads this file, applies it to the EA's CSV
These are RISK-PROCESS thresholds, not a profit target. Passing them means
'the execution behaved as designed on this sample', never 'this is
profitable'. Nothing here is a forecast, a win rate or a promise.
The defaults are the values agreed in the v6.6.24 audit brief; they are
deliberately tight because the trial exists to catch defects, not to

notes.min_trades: Fewer closed trades than this and every statistic below is noise. analyze_trial.py still prints the numbers and marks the verdict INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS.
notes.max_dd_r: Worst peak-to-trough drawdown of the cumulative R curve, in R. Zero means a straight line up (possible on 3 trades, meaningless). This is the number the owner checks FIRST: a strategy with positive expectancy and a 9R drawdown is not tradable at this account size.
notes.min_expectancy_r: Mean R per closed trade. 0.0 means break-even before costs; the trial must at least not lose money in R terms to continue.
notes.max_avg_slippage_points: Mean |fill price - planned entry price| in points, from the fill rows. Above this, the plan being tested is not the plan being executed and the trial is measuring the broker, not the strategy.
notes.min_sample_for_conclusion: Below this many closed trades the tool prints 'sample size too small to conclude' even when every threshold passes. That sentence is part of the deliverable, not a caveat.
